items.instructions: Choose the idiom that matches each definition.
options: hit the nail on the head

items.prompt: to stop working because you have done enough for now

explanation.en: Call it a day means to stop an activity, usually work, for the time being.

items.prompt: to do something unpleasant that you have been putting off

explanation.en: Bite the bullet means to accept that you must do something difficult and just do it.

items.prompt: to reveal a secret by accident or too soon

explanation.en: Spill the beans means to let a secret out. It is informal and often playful.

items.prompt: to describe a situation or problem in exactly the right way

explanation.en: Hit the nail on the head means to say something that is exactly right.
Under the weather means a little unwell. It is milder than saying you are ill.

items.instructions: Complete each sentence with the best idiom.

items.prompt: The row over who ate the last biscuit was ___ and was forgotten by lunchtime.

explanation.en: A storm in a teacup is a lot of fuss about something unimportant.

items.prompt: Heavy metal is ___, I'm afraid; I much prefer jazz.

explanation.en: Not my cup of tea is a polite way to say you do not like something.

items.prompt: It took her a month to ___ the new accounting system.

explanation.en: Get the hang of means to learn how to do something. It is followed directly by the thing you learn.

items.prompt: Our new receptionist is always ___, so nothing is ever forgotten.

explanation.en: On the ball means alert and quick to notice and deal with things.

items.prompt: We hear from our cousins in Australia only ___.

explanation.en: Once in a blue moon means very rarely.
